text: Mrs. Straker's further statements: the knife, Derbyshire
why: The story has not mentioned 'Derbyshire' at all. So far Mrs. Straker has said only that the knife lay on the dressing-table.
Mrs. Straker woke to find him dressing, and he took the knife from the dressing-table as he left the room. That room is plainly their bedroom.
The Inspector mentions the cork disk guarding the tip, found beside the body.
The wife says the knife had lain upon the dressing-table.

text: What was Straker's knife for? — as a weapon
why: The Inspector suggests Straker took it as the best weapon he could lay his hands on.
